default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1488.title: Same-minute seasonal drift follow
E-1488.hypothesis: A given minute of the day tends to carry the same sign of forward drift over the last 20 sessions (scheduled flows: opening, lunch, US open); when the average forward return is consistent, ride it.

E-1489.title: CUSUM drift detection follow
E-1489.hypothesis: A one-sided cumulative sum of returns above a drift allowance detects a persistent order flow earlier than a fixed lookback; slow positions keep building after the detection.

E-1490.title: Volume-weighted vs simple mean spread cross
E-1490.hypothesis: When the volume-weighted mean price rises above the simple mean, the volume is trading at higher prices than the time average: buyers are the aggressive side.

E-1491.title: Absorption bar at a window extreme
E-1491.hypothesis: Heavy volume per point of range at a new window low (high) with the close in the upper (lower) half means passive orders absorbed the aggressors; trade the other way.

E-1492.title: Flat-close stall break
E-1492.hypothesis: A string of closes inside a very narrow band means both sides wait; the first close beyond the band shows who gave up and the move carries.

E-1493.title: Prior-close excursion break
E-1493.hypothesis: Distance travelled from yesterday's settlement beyond what is normal for this minute of the day marks directional repricing of overnight information; follow the first crossing.

E-1494.title: Harami reversal after a big bar
E-1494.hypothesis: A small opposite bar contained inside a large bar's body shows the large bar's push has lost follow-up; its late participants are trapped.

E-1495.title: Smoothed close-location cross
E-1495.hypothesis: The average position of closes within their own bar ranges shows persistent buying or selling pressure independent of volume; follow when it becomes one-sided.

E-1496.title: Bounce through the prior bar after a typical-size drop
E-1496.hypothesis: After a normal-size move in one direction, a bar against it closing through the previous bar's extreme after a counter-colour bar marks the end of the push; trade the reversal.

E-1497.title: Wide bar closing beyond the window's closes
E-1497.hypothesis: A bar whose range is above average plus a number of sd that also closes beyond every close of the window is a range expansion with direction; follow it.
